solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Company ordered to keep extremely slow breed of sheep

parts.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to be ordered to do something is to be told to

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters, so only the two ends are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of slow

explanation.surface: A farming firm is instructed to rear a particularly sluggish kind of sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads like an adjective describing the company, but it is the past participle meaning told, which then holds the ends of slow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cotswold is a long-woolled English sheep breed named after the hills in Gloucestershire where it was raised.

clue.text: Violent storm in progress splitting bike

indicators.note: something that splits a thing sits in the middle of it, so one piece is lodged inside another

parts.note: a cycle is a bike
an event that is on is happening now

explanation.surface: A fierce storm is under way and tearing a bicycle apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In progress' looks like part of the storm description, but it supplies the short word that sits inside the bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclone is a powerful rotating weather system with destructive winds, a type of violent storm.

clue.text: Duke at the bottom of quaint British river

indicators.note: in a down answer the bottom is the end, so this piece is placed after the other

parts.note: twee means affectedly quaint or dainty
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A duke has sunk to the bottom of a charming British river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the bottom of' only works because this is a down clue: the duke's letter goes below, so last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river flowing through the Scottish Borders and forming part of the boundary between Scotland and England.

clue.text: Maybe activity in the main secure: daughter browsing the Net

parts.note: to secure a prize is to win it
D is the abbreviation for daughter
browsing the internet is called surfing

explanation.surface: Probably the main thing to make safe is a daughter spending hours online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic name for the open sea, not 'chiefly'; 'Maybe' warns that this is just one example of a sea activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsurfing, riding a board with a sail across the water, is one example of a sport practised out on the sea.

clue.text: The French on journey behave uncontrollably

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing sitting on another lies above it, so this piece comes first

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: French holidaymakers on a trip run wild.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break moves: LE plus TRIP is read as LET RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: To let rip is an informal idiom for acting or speaking without any restraint, losing all control.

clue.text: Goddess lives twice

indicators.note: twice asks for the same piece to be written down two times in a row

parts.note: one who lives is, exists
the same piece again

explanation.surface: A goddess gets two lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives' is a verb here, meaning exists, not the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was a major deity of ancient Egyptian religion, worshipped as mother and protector.

clue.text: Animated chap starts to notice inner strength — eating this veg?

indicators.note: animated means lively and moving, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A cartoon sailor finds hidden strength by eating a particular vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The animated chap is Popeye, the cartoon sailor who gains strength from cans of this vegetable; 'Animated' also does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinach is a leafy green vegetable, the very food Popeye swallows for his sudden power.

clue.text: Cut small tree

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
teak is a tropical hardwood tree

explanation.surface: Fell a little tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb acting on the tree, but it is a noun: a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A steak is a thick slice of beef or fish, the kind of portion a butcher calls a cut.

clue.text: Remove dirt from lance frantically

indicators.note: acting frantically means flailing wildly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs grime off a lance in a hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase verb, so the answer is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean something is to wash away grime or mess, making it free of muck.

clue.text: White insect hidden in foliage Tim retrieved from the rear

indicators.note: reading from the rear means starting at the back, so the letters run backwards
something hidden in words lies concealed within their run of letters

parts.note: the end of foliage, all of Tim, and the start of retrieved

explanation.surface: Tim fishes a pale bug out of the back of some leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across three words and must be read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Termites are pale wood-eating insects often called white ants because of their colour and colonies.

clue.text: Public school blue regularly fit for sport

parts.note: Rugby is a famous English public (private fee-paying) school

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of blue
an ague is a fit of fever and shivering

explanation.surface: A sporty public schoolboy who has won a blue is regularly fit enough for games.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a public school is a private fee-paying one, and Rugby school gave its name to the game; 'fit' is a noun, a bout of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby league is the thirteen-a-side form of rugby football, a team game played with an oval ball.

clue.text: Aged heads of organisation leave dutifully

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, so only the openings are kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Elderly bosses of a company retire obediently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' looks like the bosses of the firm, but it means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged and old both describe someone who has lived for many years.

clue.text: Heather tracks singular, stern type of footwear

indicators.note: to track something is to follow it, so this piece comes after the other

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
ling is another name for common heather
the stern of a ship is its back

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather follows a lone, severe kind of shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant; 'stern' is the noun for the rear of a boat, not severe.
explanation.definitionFit: A slingback is a shoe held on by a strap around the heel rather than enclosing it.

clue.text: Complete set of religious books found in Ireland

indicators.note: something found in a place lies inside it, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A full collection of scripture turns up in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete set' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Complete' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Complete and entire both mean whole, with no part missing.

clue.text: Wreck games lesson after teacher finally stops commotion

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, filling its middle, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion

indicators.note: after means following on, so this piece comes behind the other
finally points to the very end, so only the last letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of teacher
PE is physical education, the school games lesson

explanation.surface: A PE class run by a teacher puts an end to some rowdiness and ruins things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' is a verb here: to sink or ruin something.
explanation.definitionFit: To torpedo a plan is to sabotage it, a figurative use of sinking a ship with an underwater missile.

clue.text: Line of punctuation initially helps you write about Henry

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to pen a letter is to write it
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark first helps you write about a man named Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is the SI unit of inductance, written H, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a short dash used to join words or split them at the end of a printed row.

clue.text: Artless character spoilt Evita in New York

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York

indicators.note: something spoilt is damaged and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A guileless performer ruins a production of the musical Evita on Broadway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artless character' sounds like a person, but it is a trait: the quality of being artless.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence and lack of guile, so an artless disposition is exactly that quality.

clue.text: Comic actor Stan's wreath of honour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Stan of the comedy double act with Oliver Hardy
second meaning: the crown of bay leaves awarded to victors

explanation.surface: A famous comedian is presented with a garland of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive makes one phrase of what are two separate meanings of one surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan Laurel was the slapstick film comedian; a laurel is also a victor's crown of bay leaves, a symbol of distinction.

clue.text: The grime developed around a secluded abode

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps another
something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Dirt has built up around a lonely dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Developed' sounds like the grime spreading, but it signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermitage is the remote dwelling of a hermit, someone living alone away from society.

clue.text: Army beginning to approach plant

parts.note: a host is an old word for an army or a great multitude

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the first letter of approach

explanation.surface: An army starts to advance on a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory under attack, but it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The hosta is a shade-loving garden perennial grown for its broad leaves.

clue.text: Quietly welcome Greek character

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
hi is a word of greeting

explanation.surface: Someone softly greets a person from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet, a written symbol.

clue.text: Man on board catches right shellfish

indicators.note: to catch something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a pawn is a chess man, a piece on the board
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sailor on deck hauls in the correct seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' looks like a crew member on a ship; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small edible crustacean, one of the creatures sold as shellfish.

clue.text: Mum and Georgia brought in stray horse of renown

parts.note: mum means silent, as in keep mum, and sh is a call for silence

indicators.note: something brought in is taken inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: to err is to stray from what is right
GA is the US state abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: A mother and her daughter Georgia take in a famous runaway horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not a mother but the word for silent; 'stray' is a verb, to wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Shergar was a celebrated Derby-winning racehorse, famously kidnapped in Ireland in 1983 and never found.

clue.text: Pleased with English open space in woodland

indicators.note: with means alongside, so this piece is set next to the other

parts.note: to be glad is to be pleased
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An Englishman is happy to find a clearing among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' looks like part of the phrase 'pleased with', but it only sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A glade is a clearing, a patch of grass with no trees, within a forest.

clue.text: Charlie leaves a preliminary exam in a frenzy

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are no longer there, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: a mock is a British practice exam sat before the real one
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie storms out of a practice exam in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like Charlie walking out of the exam, but it removes his letter. In British schools a mock is a trial exam before the real one.
explanation.definitionFit: To run amok is to behave wildly and out of control, so the adverb means frenziedly.

clue.text: Tree unknown on northeastern island

indicators.note: in an across clue a piece on another is tacked after it, so it comes later

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
NE is the abbreviation for northeastern
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown quantities

explanation.surface: An unidentified tree grows on an island off the northeast coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northeastern island' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'island' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands, lying off the coast of Normandy.
